scope_drift_notes: Included a one-time Tier 1 backfill (project manifest/mission/rules + architecture + roadmap had never been written to Engram for this mature repo) as a prerequisite, not itself part of the feature scope - future Tier 2/3 changes on this project will not repeat that cost. Mid-flight product decisions: AMB-001 (cached-ref-by-default vs auto-fetch vs opt-in flag, resolved to opt-in flag) surfaced during requirements capture. sdd-tasks' Review Workload Forecast revised the entry contract's advisory single-pr/single-batch recommendation to chained-pr/two-batch after estimating ~430-470 changed lines. One extra fix beyond the original 20 tasks.md items was added mid-PR2: a judgment-day-found ACTION-hint gap (backend said 'in sync (healthy)' while the status badge correctly showed 'behind origin') was fixed under RED-then-GREEN TDD at user's explicit request, since it was single-judge/WARNING and did not meet the both-judges-CRITICAL auto-fix bar on its own.
variance_vs_plan: The pre-start estimate (sdd/sync-check-repo-behind-origin/estimate, obs #2071) was 14-24h, calibrated as traditional human-effort hours. Measured agent-compute-time is a different, smaller unit (~1.4h across ~26 delegated sub-agent calls, accounting for parallel judge pairs) and is not directly comparable to the estimate's basis. total_wall_clock_hours is corrected from 1.4 to approximately 36 hours (~1.5 calendar days). THIS FIGURE IS RECONSTRUCTED FROM THE CLOSURE NARRATIVE, NOT MEASURED: no timestamp instrumentation captured elapsed wall-clock time at record-close, so the value is a best-estimate reconstruction spanning tiering go-ahead through archive, including the provider rate/session-limit interruption (session reset around 12:30am UTC, resumed the next calendar day) - it is an approximation, not a conservative lower bound and not a direct measurement. checkpoint_count is corrected to 12 (previously omitted), itemized from the closure narrative: tiering go-ahead (1, durably observed via pipeline-state) + AMB-001 ambiguity clarifying question (1, durably observed via pipeline-state, surfaced during requirements capture, before the proposal phase) + proposal-decision confirmations (3, reconstructed from narrative) + judgment-day y/n rounds (4, reconstructed from narrative) + chained-PR split confirmation (1, reconstructed from narrative) + merge authorization (1, reconstructed from narrative) + ACTION-hint fix scope confirmation (1, reconstructed from narrative) = 12. Durable floor: 2 of 12 (tiering go-ahead + AMB-001 ambiguity clarifying question, both durably observed via pipeline-state per the R-006 floor). Reconstructed from narrative: 10 of 12 (proposal-decision confirmations, judgment-day rounds, chained-PR split confirmation, merge authorization, ACTION-hint fix scope confirmation) - none of these were captured in agent compute-time but they were the actual throughput bottleneck, not implementation effort. Calibration takeaway for future AI-orchestrated SDD changes on this project: track agent-compute-time, elapsed-calendar-time, and checkpoint-count as three independent units - do not blend them, and do not treat a large variance between compute-time and calendar-time as a planning miss.
